Getting started with mongolmaps

Source: vignettes/mongolmaps.Rmd
mongolmaps.Rmd

mongolmaps provides boundaries, place names and mapping helpers for Mongolia. The simplified boundaries are included in the package, so the examples below work without internet access.

Install the packages once:

install.packages(c("mongolmaps", "ggplot2"))

Your first map 

library(mongolmaps)
library(ggplot2)

mn_map(mn_aimags(), title = "Mongolia: aimags and Ulaanbaatar")

mn_aimags() gets the boundaries. mn_map() draws them and returns a ggplot, which you can change with the usual ggplot2 functions.

Choose the right boundaries

Mongolia has 21 aimags (provinces) and the capital, Ulaanbaatar. Aimags contain soums, which contain bags. Ulaanbaatar contains districts (duureg), which contain khoroos.

What you need Function Included?
Country outline mn_country() Yes
Four economic regions and Ulaanbaatar mn_regions() Yes
21 aimags and Ulaanbaatar mn_aimags() Yes
330 soums and 9 city districts mn_soums() Yes
Ulaanbaatar outline mn_ub() Yes
Nine city districts mn_ub_districts() Yes
204 khoroos mn_khoroos() Yes, unofficial boundaries
Rural bags mn_bags() Names and codes; supply your own boundaries

These functions return an sf object: a table with a geometry column that stores the shapes. Useful columns include pcode (a unique place code), name, nso_code, parent_pcode and area_km2.

aimags <- mn_aimags()
knitr::kable(head(sf::st_drop_geometry(aimags)[c("name", "pcode", "nso_code")]))
name pcode nso_code
Ulaanbaatar MN11 511
Dornod MN21 421
Sukhbaatar MN22 422
Khentii MN23 423
Tuv MN41 341
Govisumber MN42 342

Use name_en, name_mn or name_mns for English, Cyrillic Mongolian or Latin Mongolian names. Names and codes explains the codes and spelling variants.

Show part of the country

Select places with aimag or region. Common spelling variants work too.

west <- mn_soums(aimag = c("Khovd", "Uvs", "Bayan-Ulgii"))
mn_map(west, title = "Soums in western Mongolia")

Use mn_aimags(region = "Western") for the whole western region. Labels are easier to read when you show one aimag at a time.

Add towns, rivers and neighbouring countries

These small background layers are included in the package.

mn_map(mn_regions(), fill = name, context = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(
    data = mn_settlements(type = c("capital", "aimag_centre")),
    colour = "firebrick", size = 1
  ) +
  labs(title = "Economic regions and aimag centres", fill = "Region",
       caption = paste(strwrap(mn_citation(c("admin", "naturalearth", "settlements")), width = 95), collapse = "\n"))

Use Mongolian labels 

mn_map(mn_aimags(), label = TRUE, lang = "mn", label_size = 2.5)

Set options(mongolmaps.lang = "mn") to use Mongolian names by default. If Cyrillic letters appear as boxes, choose a font that supports them, for example + theme_mn(base_family = "Arial").

Coordinates and detail

Boundaries use longitude and latitude (EPSG:4326). mn_map() chooses a suitable projection for display. Use mn_aimags(crs = "albers") for national equal-area coordinates or mn_ub(crs = "utm") for Ulaanbaatar in UTM zone 48N.

The included shapes are simplified for fast plotting. This optional command downloads full-resolution boundaries once and saves them for later use. It needs internet access the first time.

khovd <- mn_soums(aimag = "Khovd", resolution = "high")

Where to go next

  • Put your data on a map.
  • Map Ulaanbaatar districts and khoroos.
  • Add roads, water and settlements.
  • Map elevation, land cover and population grids.

mn_sources() lists providers and licences. Use mn_citation() for credit text. Khoroo boundaries and the district lines derived from them are unofficial; a source snapshot does not establish their effective date.
